result.summary: This PR adds accounting in init.cpp for file descriptors consumed by IPC: one per -ipcbind listening socket plus a configurable -ipcmaxconnections (default 16) reservation for accepted connections, since neither was previously counted in min_required_fds. It adds a functional test (interface_ipc_init.py) asserting the new startup log line reporting the FD reservation, and a warning when -ipcmaxconnections is set without -ipcbind. The author has since drafted an alternative PR (#35037) that instead adds per-address max-connections options to -ipcbind, and marked this PR as draft in favor of that approach.
result.problem: Before this change, IPC listening sockets and accepted connections were not counted when the node reserves file descriptors at startup, so IPC-heavy workloads could exhaust available FDs at unpredictable moments, producing confusing failures for operators using -ipcbind.

open_concerns: Whether to reserve FDs via a new global -ipcmaxconnections option (this PR) or via per-address max-connections on -ipcbind (#35037), pending a related libmultiprocess API (bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#269) that would let per-listener limits actually be enforced.
sedited questioned whether per-bind FD accounting granularity is overkill; author responded but no fix implemented.
ryanofsky noted an unrelated behavior change (no longer reserving a P2P listener FD when -listen=0) got folded in without being called out in the commit message.
resolved_concerns: Naming of the new option was iterated (-unixmaxconnections -> -ipcmaxconnections) and settled with ryanofsky's agreement.
IsArgSet/-noipcbind negation bug flagged by ryanofsky was fixed by restructuring the logic around ipc_bind > 0.
Test placement was moved from interface_ipc_cli.py to a new interface_ipc_init.py per ryanofsky's request, and consolidated into fewer node restarts.

Severity of the FD-exhaustion problem in practice is asserted by the author and echoed generally by reviewers but not quantified with a concrete incident.
result.card: This draft PR adds file-descriptor accounting for IPC: one FD per -ipcbind listening socket and a configurable -ipcmaxconnections (default 16) for accepted connections, closing a gap where IPC FDs were previously unaccounted for and could exhaust descriptors unpredictably. It includes a focused functional test verifying the new startup log line. Reviewer ryanofsky approved the code but prefers an alternative per-address max-connections design (tracked in the author's companion draft #35037 and upstream libmultiprocess#269), and recommended this PR move to draft until that direction is decided; the author agreed and did so, though the companion PR is also still draft, leaving the two approaches unresolved. The core problem, unreserved IPC FDs, is real and acknowledged by multiple reviewers, but review effort here is paused pending a project decision between the two designs.
